messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need a clear behavior for when a primary model in a region/tier is saturated and we want to automatically surface a compatible variant. Do we treat this as a transparent reroute (no user-visible change) or an explicit fallback that we annotate and bill differently?
aj: +1 on deciding semantics. Ops needs deterministic routing. My preference: transparent reroute only for compatible-accuracy variants within same tier; otherwise explicit fallback.
devin: Product question: customers care about cost/accuracy. If we silently switch to a cheaper quantized variant and it degrades quality, that's a support headache. I'd rather we expose a per-tenant toggle: `allow_auto_variant_fallback` with default = false for enterprise.
nina: Telemetry: either way we need events for `fallback.triggered`, `fallback.type` (capacity|latency|error), `fallback.from_model`, `fallback.to_model`, `fallback.reason_code`, and `fallback.client_impact` (latency_delta, tokens_changed). Also console chart showing fallback rate by tenant/model/region.
samir: Operationally, we also need a circuit-breaker so repeated fallbacks for a tenant escalate to rate-limiting or traffic isolation. If primary keeps filling up, we should prefer draining requests to dedicated spare capacity, not bouncing between variants.
kevin: Console UX idea: in the model routing page show a toggle per-model: "Auto fallback to compatible variants" with a small dialog describing guarantees (same accuracy band / maybe 95th quant behavior). Also expose a timeline of fallbacks and a link to sample responses for quick QA.
aj: Routing API semantics proposal: add `X-Redwood-Route-Preference` header with values: `prefer_primary`, `allow_variant_fallback`, `allow_region_diversion`. Default server-side behavior uses tenant config + header. If `prefer_primary` and primary is saturated return 429 rather than fallback.
maria: Sounds good. We should also document billing: if we fall back to a cheaper variant, do we bill at cheaper model rate or at original requested model rate? Legal + billing need to weigh here. For now proposal: bill by actual served model; surface a `served_model_id` in response header for auditing.
devin: From product POV: require an opt-in for default-free accounts to auto-fallback to lower-quality variants. For PLG tiers maybe allow it because they opt into cost-saving defaults.
nina: Quick example telemetry payload I want from runtime when a fallback happens:
```
{ event: "fallback.triggered", tenant: "acct_123", from: "gptx-8k", to: "gptx-8k-quant", reason: "capacity_saturation", region: "us-west-2", tier: "standard", latency_before_ms: 180, latency_after_ms: 95 }
```
kevin: Regarding UI controls: add a per-tenant override (console + API) and a global default config in org settings. Also allow a short-circuit in the console to simulate a fallback for QA.
samir: Ops note: autoscaler needs a signal from routing that we're doing excessive fallbacks so we can inject emergency capacity. Suggest `fallback_rate` metric per model-region that feeds emergency scaling policy.
autoscaler-bot: [autoscaler] alert: model gptx-8k us-west-2 primary saturation detected — fallback rate 12% over 5m. Suggested action: +2 nodes reserved.
aj: Implementation sketch for router (very rough):
```
# routing decision pseudocode
if tenant_config.allow_variant_fallback or request_header == 'allow_variant_fallback':
  if primary.saturation():
    candidate = pick_compatible_variant(primary, tenant_constraints)
    if candidate and candidate.capacity > threshold:
      route_to(candidate)
      emit_event('fallback.triggered', ...)
      set_response_header('X-Redwood-Served-Model', candidate.id)
      return
# fallback not allowed or no candidate
if primary.saturation():
  if tenant_config.allow_region_diversion:
    route_to(compatible_primary_in_other_region)
  else:
    return 429
```
maria: Two further questions: 1) how do we decide "compatible"? (accuracy bands, perplexity delta on eval set, or model family)? 2) what SLA promises do we owe if we divert across region?
aj: Compatibility: we should use a model-compatibility matrix maintained when we onboard models (e.g., `compatibility_score(primary, candidate)`), threshold per-tenant. For SLA: cross-region diversion implies potential latency/regulatory implications — require tenant opt-in for cross-region fallback.
devin: Also add a visible flag in response payload `metadata.fallback_reason` for customers who want to log it client-side. Might be optional for performance-sensitive flows.
samir: On the circuit-breaker, store a sliding window counter per tenant+primary_model; if fallback_rate > X% for Y minutes, mark tenant as "degraded" and throttle or move to reserved capacity.
kevin: UX acceptance criteria: 1) clear console toggle, 2) fallback histogram by model/tenant/region, 3) link from graph -> sample trace showing exact request/response pair for a fallback.
maria: Action items: aj to prototype router headers and response header; nina to prototype telemetry + console graph contract; kevin to mock UI; devin to update product policy for opt-in; samir to define circuit-breaker thresholds and escalation.
aj: I'll open a PR with `X-Redwood-*` header changes and a staging flag today.
devin: I'll draft policy text and sample billing wording (bill by served model, but surface credits or warnings).
nina: I'll add telemetry schema and a Grafana dashboard skeleton in the observability repo.
samir: I'll propose circuit-breaker numbers after looking at current fallback distributions.
kevin: I'll add a mock in Figma and link in the thread.
maria: Great — thanks everyone. We'll sync next week after PR + mocks. :thumbsup:
